newsitem.title: USA: U.S. north Plains snowstorm cuts power to 26,000.
newsitem.headline: U.S. north Plains snowstorm cuts power to 26,000.

text.p: At least 26,000 homes and businesses were without electricity Monday morning in Minnesota and North Dakota after the area was slammed by a severe weekend ice, snow and wind storm, officials said.

"It was a very severe storm," said Lee Krogh, spokesman for Otter Tail Power Co, which delivers power to about 124,000 customers through eastern North Dakota, western Minnesota and northeastern South Dakota.
About 20,000 to 25,000 Otter Tail customers, primarily in eastern North Dakota, were without power Monday due to the storm, which hit Saturday and continued through Sunday, Krogh said.
Northern States Power Co was estimated to have about 4,000 customers without power in North Dakota and Minnesota as of Monday morning.
"We had about 13,000 (customers) out at the peak of the storm (early Sunday)," said Northern States spokeswoman Gaye Jaenchen.
Northern States serves about 1.4 million customers in Minnesota, Wisconsin, North and South Dakota and Michigan.
Utilities in the area were just today beginning to assess the storm impact, officials said, with significant damage expected to both major power lines and local distribution lines.
Many roads remained impassable early Monday, and snow continued to hamper visibility, Jaenchen said.
"We have reports of transmission and distribution lines down, but our crews have not yet been able to make a full assessment," the spokeswoman said.
It was not yet known when remaining Northern States customers would have electricity service returned, she said.
"We've got two planes in the air right now to assess the damage," Otter Tail's Krogh said, adding "until we find that (damage) out, we don't know where or with what equipment to send our crews out."

Rain which began Saturday turned to ice and then snow, weighing down power lines in severe winds. In Bismark, N.D., the storm brought an estimated 18 to 24 inches of snow with winds of 40 to 60 miles per hour.
The spring snowstorm followed a hard winter for the area with above-normal snow and cold temperatures.
"This snowstorm brings to 116 inches the amount of snow we've had in the area this winter, we have never broke 100 (inches) before in recorded history," Krogh said from Fergus Falls, Minn.
"We're the frozen chosen, with eight foot high drifts," said John Brookhart, spokesman for MDU Resources Group Inc subsidiary Montana-Dakota Utilities Co, headquartered in Bismark, N.D.
Brookhart estimated about 2,000 to 3,000 of Montana-Dakota's electricity customers in western North Dakota, eastern Montana and northern South Dakota were without power.

"Our main problems are in towns with 2,000 or less population," Brookhart said, adding that almost all Montana-Dakota Utilities' customers were expected to have electricity restored by Monday evening.
